en: The Banaue Rice Terraces act as giant inclined planes, reducing the force needed to carry farming tools up the steep Cordillera mountains.
Filipino fishermen use a bamboo pole as a first-class lever to lift heavy fishing nets out of Manila Bay.
Treads on Jeepney tires increase friction against the wet asphalt of EDSA, preventing the vehicle from skidding during heavy monsoon rains.
Gravity pulls the water of the Pasig River downward, ensuring it flows westward into Manila Bay.
The black sand beaches of Ilocos contain magnetite, a magnetic mineral that can be attracted to a lodestone.
The MakBan geothermal power plant in Laguna converts heat energy from underground volcanic steam into electricity for Filipino homes.
Sunlight provides the radiant energy that rice plants in Nueva Ecija need to perform photosynthesis and grow grains.
Striking the brass kulintang gongs in Maguindanao creates sound waves that travel through the air to reach the audience's ears.
Thermal energy transfers through conduction when a metal spoon heats up while stirring hot arroz caldo in a bowl.
Water stored high behind the dam at Maria Cristina Falls possesses gravitational potential energy before dropping to spin turbines.
The wooden wheels and central axle of a traditional kalesa in Vigan reduce friction to transport passengers smoothly.
Pounding unhusked palay with a heavy wooden pestle in a lusong transforms kinetic energy into sound and heat.
